 Log in Cardinals non-tender former first-round pick Nolan Gorman (report)
 45 minutes ago MLB.com
 Share share-square--:R1qlq: The Cardinals have opted not to tender a contract to Nolan Gorman ahead of Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline, according to a report from MLB Network insider Joel Sherman.
 The club has not confirmed the move.
 Gorman was entering his second year of arbitration with the club. The 26-year-old infielder was a first-round pick by St. Louis in 2018 (19th overall) and made his big league debut as a 22-year-old in 2022.

 His best season came in 2023 when he played 119 games and hit 27 homers with 76 RBIs and seven stolen bases. His playing time dropped in '26, when he appeared in a career-low 85 games, mostly due to top prospect JJ Wetherholt making his big league debut and becoming a mainstay in the lineup. 
 Gorman now becomes a free agent and could be sought after by teams looking for a utility player who has power potential. He has played second base, third base, first base, left field and designated hitter throughout his big league career.
